title: Anatomy of a workflow
summary: on, jobs, runs-on, steps, uses and run: reading a workflow file line by line.

steps.title: Where workflows live
body: A GitHub Actions **workflow** is a YAML file in `.github/workflows/`. GitHub reads every file there and runs the ones whose trigger matches.
name: ci                     # shown in the Actions tab
runs-on: ubuntu-latest   # a fresh virtual machine per job
- run: dotnet build             # a shell command
Every job gets a **clean machine**. Nothing on disk survives from one job to the next unless you pass it as an artifact.

steps.prompt: Job `build` runs `dotnet publish -o out`. Job `deploy` then runs `ls out` and gets *No such file or directory*. Why?
options: Each job runs on its own fresh runner; files must be passed with upload/download-artifact
steps.explain: Jobs do not share a filesystem. Upload in one job, download in the next (and add `needs: build`).

steps.title: uses vs run
body: - `run:` a shell command (bash on Linux, PowerShell on Windows runners). Multi-line with `|`.
- `uses:` an **action**: reusable code at `owner/repo@ref`, configured with `with:`.
`@v6` is a tag the action's author can move. Module 5 shows why security-sensitive repos pin a full commit SHA instead.

steps.prompt: Complete the workflow so it runs on pushes to `main` and on pull requests, on Ubuntu.
steps.explain: `on` holds the triggers, `runs-on` picks the runner image, `steps` is a list, and `uses` pulls in an action.

steps.prompt: Match each trigger to when it fires.
pairs: commits arrive on a branch or tag
a PR is opened or updated

steps.title: Branch filters
body: Triggers can be narrowed with glob filters:
So `release/*` matches `release/1.2` but not `release/1.2/hotfix`; `release/**` matches both.

steps.prompt: The filter is `branches: ['release/*']`. Pushes arrive on these branches. Type the ones that trigger the workflow, one per line, in the same order.
steps.explain: `*` stops at `/`, so the hotfix branch does not match; `release-2.1` has no slash at all.

steps.prompt: Arrange the job's steps in the order they must run.
steps.explain: Get the code, install the SDK, then restore, build, test. `--no-restore` and `--no-build` skip work done by the previous step.

steps.title: Match branch filters
prompt: Write `bool BranchMatches(string pattern, string branch)` implementing GitHub's two wildcards:
- `*` matches zero or more characters except `/`
- `**` matches zero or more characters including `/`
- every other character must match exactly, and the whole branch must match.
hints: Translate the pattern into a regex: `**` → `.*`, `*` → `[^/]*`, everything else `Regex.Escape`d.
Anchor with `^` and `$` so the whole branch name must match.
template: Dojo.Eq("main does not match main2", false, BranchMatches("main", "main2"));
Dojo.Eq("release/* stops at a slash", false, BranchMatches("release/*", "release/1.2/hotfix"));
